page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 31.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a single 137 GB NVMe SSD. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

The Intel Xeon processor operates at a base speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a 504 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning operations. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, achieving 35.55 GB/sec in gzip compression and a top-tier score of 2828.0 in Geekbench text processing. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall within the average range.

Multi-core and memory subsystem performance present notable tradeoffs. The server's multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, are positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a significant bottleneck, with read-only large block bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% at 22.46 GB/sec, and write large block bandwidth in the bottom 25% at 15.13 GB/sec. Additionally, static web serving throughput and Passmark database operations are relatively weak.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and built-in NVMe SSD, this server is structured for memory-intensive tasks that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suitable for Redis caching, single-threaded text processing, and light database operations where local SSD speed is beneficial. The inclusion of AMX allows for moderate small-model LLM inference, though text generation on medium models is poor. The hardware profile offers a qualitative balance of high memory capacity and fast local storage on a low vCPU footprint, though memory bandwidth limitations should be factored into resource planning.
